gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-phoenicia: Edo SZ draws every stroke at a single constant width, with lowercase that stands like cast iron capitals. Noto Sans Phoenician follows in a modern, generous-height sans whose s curves open wide at both ends.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-psalter-p: Edo SZ looks traced with one marker, its lowercase standing tall like cast iron capitals, while Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi gapes open on the e. Body text could go a notch larger.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Wire-straight, cast-iron confident. Edo SZ holds one stroke width throughout, while Noto Sans Rejang gives its lowercase wide, porthole-like counters and clear gaps in c, e, s and a.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-runic: Edo SZ bends its letters like paperclip wire, with no thick-thin shifts anywhere in its tall lowercase. Noto Sans Runic then brings a big x-height and curves that never close back on themselves.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Edo SZ keeps an unvarying weight from word to word, its lowercase as tall as cast iron capitals. And Noto Sans Samaritan does the opposite job, a hefty sans-serif lowercase with plenty of daylight inside its curves.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-saurashtr: Classic and cultural, Edo SZ pulls its lowercase like drawn wire, tall as cast iron capitals. Noto Sans Saurashtra offers the clean opposite, capitals barely above their neighbors and counters left connected to the outside.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-sc: Edo SZ has the thickness of neon glass tubing, one constant width through lowercase as tall as cast iron capitals. And Noto Sans SC can take a slightly larger size, since its chalky curves stop short of closing.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Noto Sans Sharada reads bulky and clean, its open c forms never closing into rings, and it sits under a heading drawn as tubular, wire-like letters. Edo SZ brings the cast iron stature.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Not one hairline anywhere, even in the lowercase a. Noto Sans Siddham adds a large central band and an s with ends hanging far from the spine, so Edo SZ gets a relaxed, modern partner.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Edo SZ writes like a ballpoint, pressure-free and constant, with lowercase as stately as cast iron capitals. Noto Sans Sinhala forms a thick dark stripe beneath it, so a slightly smaller size fits.
